definition: A fruit-like structure in which tissues beyond the ovary contribute substantially to the edible part.
A fruit structure formed from several separate ovaries of a single flower, as in raspberry.
In botany, a fleshy fruit developing from one ovary, often with seeds embedded in the pulp.
A measure of soluble solids often used as an approximate indicator of sugar content in fruit juice.
The amount of cool winter exposure some temperate plants need for normal bud break and flowering.
A fruit that generally shows a rise in respiration during ripening and may continue to ripen after harvest.
A cultivated plant selection maintained for consistent traits through appropriate propagation.
A fruit with fleshy outer tissue and a hard inner layer surrounding the seed, such as a peach.
A plant hormone involved in ripening and other developmental processes.
The coloured outer part of citrus peel, rich in aromatic oil glands.
A locally maintained crop population shaped by tradition, selection and environment.
A chamber in an ovary or fruit that may contain seeds.
A fruit that generally does not show the classic climacteric respiratory rise during ripening.
A type of berry with a hard rind, typical of cucurbits such as melons.
A fruit type in which accessory floral tissues contribute to the fleshy part, as in apples and pears.
Transfer of pollen to the receptive part of a flower, enabling fertilisation in many plants.
The rooted part of a grafted plant onto which a cultivar is joined.
The upper part of a grafted plant that determines the cultivar identity.
The hard inner layer of a drupe surrounding its seed.
A class of plant compounds that can contribute astringency in some fruits.
The aromatic coloured outer peel of citrus, used in food in small quantities.
